raw_response:
I farm 129 mu with only 2 people at home, and some labor in my family is off-farm, so I will not spread myself too thin on crops that need too much hand work. I will keep the main land in wheat-maize, because in Quzhou that is the steady road and I know how to manage it with machines and well water. I will still plant some cotton, but not too much, because cotton needs more watching, more spraying, and more picking. I will leave a small piece for millet because it is simple, does not drink too much water, and gives me one low-cost crop in case the weather turns awkward. On fertilizer, I do not like cutting too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss is bigger than the saving. So I will feed wheat and maize a bit on the safe side, especially nitrogen, but I will not go wild because every mu times 129 is real money. I will use improved seed for wheat and millet, hybrid seed for maize, and improved cotton seed. For wheat I will irrigate at least after sowing if moisture is short, then once at jointing and once at grain filling if needed. For maize I will catch the summer rain but still keep one or two well irrigations ready. Cotton I will watch for aphids, bollworm, and late disease, so spray count will be higher there. Tillage will stay practical: wheat land rotary after the last crop, maize mostly no-tillage after wheat to save time, cotton ploughed once because I want a better root zone, and millet with rotary tillage. Yield targets I will set at a level I feel I can reach on my ground, not the kind people only talk about on demonstration fields.
